_meta.note: The remaining tail of the critical review, verified present in the code, in five themed phases. KB (kernel correctness): C1 hb-lint extractPaths false-positives (sed/abspath → permanent gate_rot), C3 state.py list(set()) → nondeterministic state.json (git churn), C4 gate.py crashes on a git-less machine (no which/try guard), C8 gate_blocked re-wakes every tick with no circuit breaker. SP (safety/parse): C2 py backends' verdict is grep-anywhere `REFUTED` (11 backends) — the node fix didn't reach python, R1 doctor.py shell=True f-string path-injection, R2 node -e sites splice shell vars into JS source instead of argv. PT (portability/installed-plugin): C5 drift detection is a silent no-op on macOS (sha256sum absent, `|| true`), C6 adapter skills use repo-relative plugin/adapters/ links that 404 from an installed plugin, C7 .mcp.json declares `hb mcp-serve` a node-only install can't run, R9 no commands/ dir (/heartbeat is skill-prose). HN (honesty/coverage — the thesis): H1 no coverage floor (ALL-GREEN can lie on a stripped box), H2 the 53 planning/*.dag.json example DAGs are ungated, H3/H4 docs say '4 audit fixtures' but parity.sh uses 5 (+ any other parity-notes inaccuracy). DR (DRY/tests): R3 reason→action table duplicated, R4 non-behavioral regex forked (hb-audit.js vs hb-exec.js), R5 git-snapshot logic duplicated, R6 withWlock/with_wlock untested, R7 fixtures live in planning/ (move to tests/fixtures/), R8 mcp_server/executor scrape cli.main stdout for the review policy. Proof-driven: spec-first, gated, refuted in a stripped env; each phase keeps node/python/parity green.

phases.title: Kernel correctness — rot-lint precision, deterministic state, git-less safety, a gate_blocked breaker

tasks.title: Spec-first: proofs for the four kernel bugs
tasks.description: Author RED-first, in a stripped env: docs/howto/gate-examples/rot-lint-precision.sh (ROT-LINT-PRECISION-OK) — a gate cmd using a bash-ism like `sed 's/a/b/'` or an absolute path like `/usr/bin/node` in a COMPLETED phase does NOT trip hb-lint/doctor 'no longer reproducible', while a genuinely deleted project artifact (e.g. tests/x.js) STILL does; docs/howto/gate-examples/state-determinism.sh (STATE-DETERMINISM-OK) — two independent `rebuild`s of the same event log produce BYTE-identical state.json (completed/active/completed_phases order is stable), both runtimes; docs/howto/gate-examples/gate-gitless.sh (GATE-GITLESS-OK) — a non-review gate PASS on a machine with no `git` binary (PATH stripped) does NOT crash and still records the pass (git snapshot skipped, not fatal); docs/howto/gate-examples/gate-blocked-breaker.sh (GATE-BLOCKED-BREAKER-OK) — repeated ticks on a persistently blocked gate stop re-waking after a bounded count (a circuit breaker fires, like the no-progress breaker). All FAIL now.

tasks.title: Fix hb-lint/doctor extractPaths precision (C1)
tasks.description: In plugin/templates/hb-lint.js (and mirror in py if the rot heuristic exists there) tighten extractPaths so it only treats a token as a produced-artifact reference when it plausibly is one — exclude shell constructs (sed `s/.../.../` , flags), exclude ABSOLUTE paths (leading /), and require a relative path with a file extension or trailing slash. A completed phase whose gate uses sed or an absolute tool path must not become permanent gate_rot. Make rot-lint-precision.sh green; keep hb-lint's existing dangling-artifact tests green.

tasks.title: Deterministic state projection (C3)
tasks.description: In py/src/heartbeat/state.py, serialize completed_tasks/active_tasks/completed_phases deterministically (sorted, or insertion-ordered via dict.fromkeys) instead of list(set(...)), so state.json byte-content is stable across rebuilds and stops churning in git. Mirror in the node projector (hb.js) if it has the same nondeterminism. Make state-determinism.sh green (both runtimes); keep parity + pytest green.

tasks.title: Git-optional gate pass (C4)
tasks.description: In py/src/heartbeat/gate.py, guard EVERY git call against a missing binary — the primary crash site is run_gate (~line 80, the bare `subprocess.run(['git', … 'rev-parse','HEAD'])` for the commit) AND _git/_git_snapshot — with shutil.which('git') or try/except so a gate PASS on a git-less machine skips the snapshot/commit gracefully instead of raising FileNotFoundError ('git is optional' must hold). Mirror the guard in gate.sh if it assumes git. Make gate-gitless.sh green; keep pytest + T26/T31 git tests green.

tasks.title: gate_blocked circuit breaker (C8)
tasks.description: Add a bounded circuit breaker so a persistently blocked gate stops re-waking every tick: after N consecutive gate_blocked wakes with no state change, escalate to a distinct terminal signal (like build_stuck / no_progress) and stop re-alerting — both runtimes' resolver/tick (hb-next-task.js/tick.sh + tick.py). Make gate-blocked-breaker.sh green; keep the existing circuit-breaker tests (T6) green.

phases.title: Safety & parse — robust verdict on the python side, injection-safe subprocess/JS

tasks.title: Spec-first: verdict-robustness + injection-safety proofs
tasks.description: Author RED-first: docs/howto/gate-examples/verdict-robust.sh (VERDICT-ROBUST-OK) — a shared verdict helper decides REFUTED/CLEAR from the reply's FINAL token, so prose that merely contains the word 'REFUTED' but ends CLEAR is NOT scored as a refutation; assert via importing the python helper and feeding both orderings (matches the node claude-exec.sh fix). docs/howto/gate-examples/injection-safe.sh (INJECTION-SAFE-OK) — use REAL injection vectors, not inert ones: a project dir whose NAME contains a command-substitution `$(touch PWNED)` (which IS evaluated inside double quotes — the doctor.py:130 vector) plus a single-quote (the `node -e` JS-string breakout vector). Assert NO `PWNED` file is created by doctor.py AND the affected `node -e` sites still return correct output (don't crash/execute) — proving data is passed via argv/env, not spliced into a shell/JS source string. (A `;`-only payload is inert inside quotes and would false-pass — do not use it.) Both FAIL now.

tasks.title: Robust python verdict parse (C2)
tasks.description: Add a shared verdict helper (e.g. heartbeat.backends.base._verdict(text) → final REFUTED/CLEAR token) and route ALL py backends' refute() genuine-verdict path through it instead of `"REFUTED" in text.upper()` (11 backends). Mirrors the node fix (RV3). Make verdict-robust.sh green; keep pytest green.

tasks.title: Injection-safe subprocess + node -e (R1, R2)
tasks.description: Fix doctor.py:130 (and doctor.py:75) to pass the project path via an argv list (no shell=True f-string). Audit the `node -e` call sites across the plugin templates that splice a shell variable into the JS SOURCE and convert the ones that carry external/path data to pass it via process.argv or an env var (the safe pattern already used elsewhere in the same files). Make injection-safe.sh green; keep node + pytest suites green.

tasks.description: Author RED-first: docs/howto/gate-examples/drift-portable.sh (DRIFT-PORTABLE-OK) — the tick.sh drift hash uses a sha tool that exists on macOS too (sha256sum OR shasum fallback), and drift detection is NOT a silent no-op when sha256sum is absent (simulate by shadowing sha256sum off PATH; a changed WATCH_PATHS still yields a different hash). docs/howto/gate-examples/skill-paths.sh (SKILL-PATHS-OK) — no adapter skill under plugin/skills/*/ references a bare repo-relative `plugin/adapters/...`/`docs/...` path that would 404 from an installed plugin; they use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} or a resolvable relative link like the main skill. docs/howto/gate-examples/mcp-json-runtime.sh (MCP-JSON-RUNTIME-OK) — plugin/.mcp.json's server command is runnable by the plugin's own runtime (or the file documents/handles that `hb` must be installed), i.e. the declared command resolves or is guarded; AND the R9 command-surface decision is realized — EITHER a plugin commands/ directory registers the /heartbeat verbs, OR plugin/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md explicitly documents that /heartbeat is a skill (not commands/) so the absence is intentional — the proof asserts one of the two holds.
